latin: ausum, ausī n. · adventūra, adventūrae f.
keywords: Adventure / venture ausum, ausī n. adventūra, adventūrae f. Ancient Latin Medieval Latin Modern semantic extension ausum, ausī n. — a daring attempt, venture, undertaking or enterprise; our preferred word for modern adventure when the emphasis is on something voluntarily and boldly undertaken. adventūra, adventūrae f. — a medieval Latin word connected with what happens, chance, fortune, risk or venture; retained here as a secondary word for modern adventure by later semantic extension, especially through the Romance development of the word. Novum ausum suscipiāmus. — Let’s undertake a new adventure. Hodiē novum ausum quaerāmus. — Let’s seek a new adventure today. Nova adventūra nōs exspectat. — A new adventure awaits us; a modern-style use, not presented as an ancient idiom. The English word adventure ultimately belongs to the adventūra family, but its cheerful modern sense is later than the core medieval Latin meanings. For ordinary family speech, prefer ausum when a classical/ancient word is wanted; use adventūra when the later European word-family itself is useful.
